questions.q: Class D IP addresses are used for —
questions.solution: **Class D (224-239) = multicast groups**; Class E (240-255) is experimental.

questions.q: Which shortcut opens the Word Count dialog box?
questions.solution: Ctrl+Shift+G opens Word Count (words, characters with/without spaces, paragraphs, lines). Ctrl+Shift+C copies formatting, Ctrl+Shift+V pastes formatting, Ctrl+Shift+K formats small caps.
questions.shortcut: Word Count = Ctrl+Shift+G ('G for enGlish count' helps some aspirants).

questions.q: Meera reads her mail on her phone, tablet and laptop, and every device shows the same mailbox. Her account uses —
questions.solution: **IMAP keeps mail on the server and syncs all devices**; POP3 would strand messages on one machine.

questions.q: Which remote-login protocol sends data, including passwords, WITHOUT encryption?
questions.solution: **Telnet (23) is plaintext** — SSH (22) is its encrypted modern replacement.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

One who is easily cheated or deceived
questions.solution: One who believes too readily and is easily fooled = **gullible**. A sceptic doubts everything — almost the opposite; a cynic expects selfish motives; a pessimist expects the worst.

questions.q: The statement that a visitor to a government office 'lost a full day's wages' assumes that:
options: the visitors would otherwise have been working and earning that day
government offices pay visitors for their time
the bus fare is equal to one day's wages
government work always takes the whole day
questions.solution: Losing a day's wages only makes sense if the person would have earned money that day by working. That hidden link is the assumption. The passage says the task 'might take twenty minutes', which contradicts 'always takes the whole day'; the bus fare is never discussed; offices paying visitors is absurd and unsupported.
questions.shortcut: Negation test: if the visitors would not have been working anyway, 'lost wages' collapses — so that is the assumption.
questions.passage:
The small hill town had one bus a day to the district headquarters. It left at six in the morning and came back at seven in the evening, so anyone who needed to visit a government office lost a full day's wages for a task that might take twenty minutes. When the state began offering its certificates and forms online, the town's only cyber café suddenly had a queue outside it every morning.

The owner, a retired schoolteacher, charges ₹20 for filling a form and printing it. He says his busiest customers are elderly farmers applying for pensions and young people applying for jobs. 'Most of them have phones,' he says, 'but a small screen and a forty-page form do not go together.'

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The teacher gave the students homework.
options: The students were given homework by the teacher.
The students was given homework by the teacher.
The homework was given the students by the teacher.
The students are given homework by the teacher.
questions.solution: Double-object verb: either object can lead. 'The students were given homework by the teacher' is correct (plural → were). B breaks number; C drops the preposition 'to' ('given the students' needs 'given to the students'); D changes tense.
questions.shortcut: give offers two passives; the indirect-object one keeps 'were given'.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: The contrast is 'decoration rather than ___', and the passage argues trees are functional city assets — cooling, dust-trapping, noise-softening. The noun for functional city assets is **infrastructure**. *Entertainment, souvenir, ceremony* fit the grammar but belong to no part of the argument.
questions.shortcut: Contrast frame 'X rather than Y' wants Y from the same serious category as the argument — trees as urban equipment.
questions.passage: Concrete has conquered our cities, and the first casualty has been the tree. A mature tree on a street does more than look (1) ______: it drops the temperature of its surroundings, traps dust and softens the noise of traffic. Yet when roads are widened, it is usually the tree that (2) ______ way. Municipal budgets treat planting as decoration rather than (3) ______, so saplings are planted in a rush before elections and forgotten soon afterwards. Survival, not planting, is the real (4) ______; a sapling needs watering for three full summers before it can stand on its own. Cities that have understood this simple point now pay residents a small sum to (5) ______ the trees outside their homes — and their streets are visibly greener.

questions.q: An economy shows **rising prices along with falling output and rising unemployment**. This is —
questions.solution: **Stagflation** = stagnation (weak growth, job losses) plus inflation — the classic outcome of a severe cost-push shock, as in the 1970s oil crises.

questions.q: The headquarters of the **Ghadar Party** (Yugantar Ashram) was located in —
questions.solution: The Ghadar Party (1913), led by **Lala Har Dayal** and **Sohan Singh Bhakna**, was run from **Yugantar Ashram in San Francisco**, USA, and published the weekly *Ghadar*.
questions.shortcut: Ghadar = Indians on the **US Pacific coast** → San Francisco.

questions.q: Which alcohol is **highly poisonous** and can cause blindness?
questions.solution: **Methanol (wood spirit)** damages the optic nerve — a few teaspoons cause blindness or death. Ethanol is the ordinary alcohol of drinks.

questions.q: The **first and only woman** to rule Delhi was —
questions.solution: **Razia** (1236–1240), daughter of Iltutmish, was the first and only woman sultan of Delhi.

questions.q: When a number is divided by 195 the remainder is 47. When the same number is divided by 15, the remainder is:
questions.shortcut: Trap: 47 itself is bigger than 15, so it cannot be the remainder.

questions.q: Find the value of $1 \div \left(1 + \cfrac{1}{1 + \cfrac{1}{1 + \cfrac{1}{2}}}\right)$
questions.shortcut: The whole $1 + \frac{1}{\dots}$ block sits under the first division.

questions.q: After two equal successive discounts, an article marked at ₹6,400 is sold for ₹5,184. Each discount is:
questions.solution: Kept fraction $= \frac{5184}{6400} = 0.81 = 0.9^2$ → each discount $= 10\%$.
questions.shortcut: 9.5% halves the total 19% — successive discounts do not split evenly.

questions.q: A boat's speed in still water is 10 km/h and the stream flows at 2 km/h. The time taken to travel 24 km downstream is:
In how many different ways can **five people sit in a row** if **A and B must sit next to each other**?
questions.solution: Tie A and B into one block. Then 4 units (block, C, D, E) can be arranged in 4! = 24 ways, and inside the block A and B can swap: 24 × 2 = 48.
questions.shortcut: Block of two in a row of n: (n − 1)! × 2.

questions.q: Select the related number: **25 : 49 :: 34 : ?**
questions.solution: Digit sum of 25 is 2+5 = 7 and 7² = 49. Digit sum of 34 is 3+4 = 7, and 7² = **49**. Both members share digit sum 7 — the answer is its square again.
questions.shortcut: When a and b look unrelated, compute the digit sum: many CGL analogies are (digit sum)² or (digit sum)×k.
